title_pattern.template: Would A [Iconic Modern Animal] Survive Every [Prehistoric/Extreme Setting]?
title_pattern.type: hypothetical survival gauntlet / 'drop X into every era' question title
title_pattern.notes: Yes/no question with an implied scorecard; pairs a universally known apex animal with a time-travel tour of many eras so one video covers ~10 mini-matchups. 'Every' promises completeness and a running tally. Reusable: 'Would a T-rex survive every mass extinction?', 'Could a human survive every ice age?'

thumbnail.composition: Left 45%: huge great white head in profile facing right, cropped by frame edge, wearing a small sparkling crown. Right 50%: four prehistoric challengers (orthocone, megalodon, Dunkleosteus, mosasaur/pliosaur) arranged in a loose arc, all facing/snapping toward the shark. Title text top-centre-left.
thumbnail.text: 'Still King?' — two words, heavy condensed sans; 'Still' in white, 'King?' in red. Only ~2 words, does not repeat the title.
thumbnail.colours: Pure black background with stark black-and-white engraved/pen-and-ink (crosshatch) illustration; the only colour is the red 'King?' — very high contrast, monochrome stands out in a colourful feed.
thumbnail.subject_scale_contrast: Hero shark is 2-3x the size of each challenger and closest to camera; challengers are smaller but multiple and open-mouthed, so 'one vs many' reads instantly. Crown is a tiny prop that carries the whole premise.
thumbnail.why_it_works: Single readable question + crown prop = status challenge; open jaws on every creature promise conflict; recognisable silhouettes (megalodon, Dunkleosteus) are fan-bait for prehistoric-animal audiences. Notably the thumbnail style (engraved B&W) does NOT match the video's flat colour vector style — thumbnail is optimised purely for CTR.
thumbnail.code_remake_notes: Engraving look is hard in pure SVG; approximate with SVG hatch patterns/feTurbulence + threshold filter, or keep the brand flat-vector style and copy only the composition (big hero left + crown, 3-4 rivals right, 2-word red/white question).

hook.verbatim_0_5s: Picture the most feared animal in the sea. 6 m long, a mouth full of serrated teeth that never stop growing back.
hook.first_25s_summary: Builds up the great white with rapid superlatives (smells blood from hundreds of metres, launches seals out of the water, almost nothing attacks an adult) -> 'If any animal deserves to be called the king of the ocean, it's this one.' -> 0:23 twist: 'Except...' orcas in South Africa kill great whites with one neat wound and eat only the liver; whole coastlines empty for a year. -> 'So how much of a king is it really? Let's find out.'
hook.device: Second-person 'Picture...' imagery + stacked superlatives, then a hard subversion ('Except...') with a surprising real-world fact (orcas eating livers), which converts into the central question. Visual: hero shark side-on, then tight jaw close-up at ~6s, blood plume, backlit breach silhouette; word-by-word captions with one orange keyword.
hook.rules_setup: 0:50-1:28 sets up game rules explicitly: one adult 5 m great white, no time to adapt, must eat, one escape (can dive to 1,200 m), scoring legend crown=rules / check=survives / skull=doesn't make it. This gives the viewer a reason to stay for every era.

beats.summary: 'Picture the most feared animal in the sea' — superlative build-up of the great white as king of the ocean.
Orcas kill great whites off South Africa, eating only the liver; sharks abandon coastlines. 'How much of a king is it really?'
Drop one 5 m adult into every ocean in Earth's history; no adapting; escape = diving to 1,200 m; scoring legend crown/pass/skull.

Title card + world-building (no life on land, 21-hour days, Cambrian explosion); shark is biggest animal alive and eats Anomalocaris easily, but no big fatty prey and low oxygen -> 'king of the world and slowly starving'. Verdict SKULL (starved).
High seas, first reefs, ice cap foreshadows extinction; orthocones debunk (9 m claim vs 5.5 m real) — 'a meal with a handle'; sea scorpions snacks. Verdict CROWN.
Forests, anoxic seas, giant reefs, Tiktaalik; Cladoselache 'family'; Dunkleosteus myth-bust (2023 study ~4 m). Bone armor vs speed -> standoff. Verdict PASS. First scoreboard 1/1/1.

Giant bugs from high oxygen, coal swamps, Pangaea forms; golden age of weird sharks (Stethacanthus, Edestus, Helicoprion + fun fact it's a ratfish relative). Verdict CROWN, then Great Dying '9 in 10' kicker.
Post-extinction clean slate, ammonites, ichthyosaurs; Shonisaurus 15 m but harmless, Thalattoarchon 8.6 m apex; first time shark isn't biggest predator -> dives. Verdict PASS.

Pangaea splits, birds; pliosaurs, Liopleurodon myth-bust (25 m -> ~8 m); Leedsichthys food; pliosaurs are air-breathers so the dive saves it. Verdict PASS (IT DIVED). Scoreboard 2/3/1; 'That's about to change' cliffhanger.

Western Interior Seaway, chalk/White Cliffs, T-rex timing; mosasaurs, Tylosaurus with shark in stomach, Cretoxyrhina 'Ginsu shark' that ate mosasaurs ('Read that again'). No safe deep. Verdict SKULL (eaten).
Hothouse, palms near Arctic, whales evolve from dog-sized walkers; Basilosaurus 16 m with tiny legs, bite marks on calf skulls; shark stays deep. Verdict PASS. Teaser: 'Now the worst ocean of all.'
Upwelling food chain, swimming sloths; Megalodon (15 m, bites flippers/tail) and Livyatan (teeth on both jaws, can follow a dive). Verdict DEAD. TWICE. 'But here's where the story turns around.'

Panama closes, cooling; real great whites appear; 2022 zinc-isotope study puts early great whites at megalodon's trophic level -> may have helped push megalodon to extinction (with hedges). 'Megalodon was gone. The great white was still here.'

beats.beat_type: era 11: Modern ocean (pass, not the king)
beats.summary: Cold ocean, seals = buffet, but orcas: Farallon Islands 1997 kill, tonic immobility, sharks flee hunting grounds. Callback to the hook. 'Still running from a dolphin.' Verdict PASS - NOT THE KING.

Final tally 2 ruled / 5 survived / 3 died; rivals crossed out one by one (Dunkleosteus, pliosaurs, mosasaurs, megalodon gone); thesis: survival by knowing when to run and where to hide — 'the deep... that's what wins.'
Comment prompt 'Which animal next?' with mock comment box, then 'Watch next' end-screen card with channel logo.

avg_shot_length_s.note: ffmpeg scene>0.3 found 93 cuts (~12.7 s); scene>0.12 found 244 changes (~4.8 s). Most change happens inside shots (caption words, pop-in labels, highlight rings, element moves), so the effective 'something new on screen' interval is ~1.5-2.5 s.

pacing.segment_length: ~90-115 s per era, 10 eras + 88 s intro + ~80 s outro
pacing.structure_rhythm: Each era repeats the same 6-part template: dial transition -> era title card -> 30-45 s world-building (land, map, oxygen/climate fact) -> monster reveal with size comparison and often a myth-bust -> escape test (dive + depth gauge) -> verdict card (+ scoreboard every 2-3 eras).

visual_style.palette: Deep teal/navy underwater gradient (#0d2a3a-ish to #1f5566) with soft god rays and particles; tan/khaki landmasses (#b5a67a) with teal outlines on maps; warm sand/peach land scenes; accent gold/orange (#f2a72e) for keywords and crown; red (#e0483d) for danger words and red-tint danger states; teal (#5cc6b8) for check/oxygen bars; creatures in flat grey/white with dark outlines.
visual_style.per_era_tint: Background hue shifts per era (Cambrian greener teal, Ordovician/Jurassic deeper navy, Cretaceous brighter cyan, Miocene blue) — cheap way to signal 'new world'.
visual_style.typography: Rounded geometric sans (Raleway/Montserrat-like). Captions: lowercase white small words + ONE keyword in bold uppercase orange (or red for threat). Era cards: tiny letter-spaced 'X MILLION YEARS AGO' above 'ERANAME' bold + 'PERIOD' light. Species labels: small white text top-left with thin underline.
visual_style.characters: Single consistent flat-vector shark rig (side view, slight shading, gill slits) reused in every scene; creatures are simple layered vector cut-outs with 2-3 parts animated (jaw, tail, fins).

techniques_worth_copying: Game-show scoring frame: explicit rules + 3-icon legend (crown/check/skull) + recurring scoreboard turns a facts tour into a tournament with stakes; viewers stay to see the final tally.
Single recurring 'escape test' (can it dive deeper than the threat?) gives every segment the same decision logic and a satisfying payoff.
Era template: dial/time-machine transition -> title card -> world-building -> monster -> verdict. Very cheap to template in code and easy for viewers to follow.
Word-by-word captions with exactly one emphasised keyword per phrase (orange caps, red for danger) placed near the subject, not fixed at bottom.
Myth-bust beats: 'You might have heard it was 9 m / 25 m / 10 m... a 2023 study says 4 m' using two stacked size bars — feels smart, adds credibility.
Size-comparison panel: dark background, our hero always shown on top with a 5 m yellow ruler, challenger below with its own ruler — consistent reference object across the whole video.
Depth gauge overlay (0-1,200 m ruler with red marker) whenever the shark dives; background darkens with depth.
Colour-grade states: red tint = danger/oxygen crisis; orange 'thermal' recolour = metabolism; desaturate/fade = death.
Gold highlight rings/ellipses drawn around the anatomical detail being discussed (jaws, legs, liver).
Occasional framed real-photo cards (fossil skull, tooth, aerial photo) tilted slightly with white border to anchor claims in evidence.
Open/close bookend: hook's orca-liver twist returns at the end ('still running from a dolphin'), then a reflective thesis that reframes losing as winning.
Cliffhanger line at end of each verdict ('That's about to change', 'Now the worst ocean of all', 'But here's where the story turns around').
Comment-bait CTA with a mocked comment box: 'Which animal should we drop in next?' — feeds the series format.

code_only_remake_needs.feasibility: High. Everything is 2D flat vector with simple transforms; no camera 3D, no complex character animation. Ideal Remotion target.
assets: One reusable side-view SVG shark rig (body, jaw, tail, pectoral fin groups) with swim cycle (tail sine + body bob) and pose variants: cruise, dive (rotate ~60 deg), bite (jaw open), upside-down.
~25 creature SVGs (original designs): rivals per era; each needs 2-3 animatable parts at most.
Paleomap SVG set (Cambrian, Ordovician, Devonian, Carboniferous, Pangaea, Jurassic, Cretaceous, modern) — simplified blobs; morph between them with flubber/path interpolation.
Landscape side-view layers (sky, mountains, ground, sea strip) with swappable props (trees by era, dinosaurs, palm, dragonfly, moon).
Icon set: crown, check, skull, red X, era icons.
Optional photo cards: must be original/licensed/public-domain or replaced with drawn 'specimen' cards (do not reuse their images).
components: UnderwaterBackground: vertical gradient + animated god-ray polygons + particle drift + per-era hue prop + depth darkening prop.
KaraokeCaption: word-timed reveal from TTS/whisper word timestamps, keyword styling (orange/red uppercase bold), position prop.
EraTitleCard: 'N MILLION YEARS AGO' + bold/light era name + icon, with fade/slide.
TimeDialTransition: SVG dial with needle sweep + orange wedge wipe and logo, ~2 s.
SizeComparePanel: stacked creatures scaled to metres with animated ruler bars and labels (keeps hero as fixed reference).
DepthGauge: vertical ruler 0-N m with animated marker + label, synced to shark dive.
HighlightRing: hand-drawn-feel ellipse stroke-dash draw-on around a target bbox.
VerdictCard + Scoreboard: icon pop-in with spring, counters, per-column highlight, mini scoreboard HUD top-right.
BarStat: horizontal labelled bars (oxygen today vs then).
MapScene: framed map panel with zoom-to-region, labels, highlight circles, path morph between eras.
ColorGrade wrapper: red-danger / thermal-orange / fade-to-dark overlays.
code_only_remake_needs.pipeline: Script with per-beat storyboard JSON (era template x N) -> local TTS (Kokoro) at ~150 wpm -> word timestamps (faster-whisper) -> Remotion composition maps beats to the components above; 20-min video at 30 fps is long, so render per-era chunks on Spark CPU and concat.
code_only_remake_needs.hard_parts: Volume of creature art (~25 originals) and keeping style consistency; engraved B&W thumbnail look (use SVG hatching filters or switch to flat style thumbnail); smooth map morphs.
